text: [CG 00 01 12 07, Sec. V, ¶ 18 (emphasis added)] Thus, even assuming a potential for coverage otherwise exists, the insurer does not owe a duty to defend the insured in administrative proceedings (such as EEOC or FEHA investigations and hearings). [See Foster-Gardner, Inc. v. National Union Fire Ins. Co. (1998) 18 C4th 857, 883, 77 CR2d 107, 125—insurer owed no duty to defend insured in proceedings commenced by state Environmental Protection Agency; see also Certain Underwriters at Lloyd's of London v. Sup.Ct. (Powerine Oil Co., Inc.) ("Powerine I") (2001) 24 C4th 945, 960, 103 CR2d 672, 682—insurer's duty to indemnify insured is limited to money ordered by a court] (1) [3:486] Compare—EPL policies: This problem does not exist with standard-form Employment Practices Liability (EPL) insurance policies because coverage extends to “claims” asserted in court or administrative proceedings (see ¶ 3:216). [3:486.1 - 3:486.4] Reserved.
